requirements.evidence: Migrations match the data model (totems, totem_presets with login_code string(6) nullable unique, totem_preset_queue composite PK at create_totem_preset_queue_table.php:15-20). Command totem:pairing-code uses random_int + str_pad, sets +10 min, clears consumed_at, prints the code, writes an audit log and returns FAILURE for an unknown id (TotemPairingCode.php:17-47). Auth: 400 for a code that is not 6 digits including non-strings (TotemAuthController.php:21-28), one 401 for unknown/expired/consumed/inactive via hasUsableLoginCode (TotemPreset.php:63-70), transaction + lockForUpdate, a totem row and the {token, token_type, expires_in, entity{slug,name}} response. JWT claims and config keys, .env.example and the phpunit.xml pins are present. The middleware checks token, active state, entity consistency and the claim ∩ current-preset intersection (AuthenticateTotem.php:58-80) and calls updateQuietly for last_seen_at. Entity guard 403, queue resolved within the entity 404/403, active+ordered queues with 1-based order, priorities 0/10/20 from one source, ticket via IssueTicket with TicketChannel::Totem, 201 payload. Throttles 10/30 per minute render as rate_limited (bootstrap/app.php:44-48). CORS allow-list and a 204 preflight through an explicit OPTIONS route (routes/api.php:25-28). The IssueTicket signature is not visible in the diff but the tests exercise it.

conventions.evidence: Ticket writes go through App\Actions\IssueTicket (TotemTicketController.php:40). Models set #[Fillable] deliberately. Migrations have down() and generator-style timestamps. Docs are synced: docs/api/totem.md, architecture.md, database-schema.md, business-rules.md and CHANGELOG [Unreleased]. Deviations: the JWT helper lives in app/Services/TotemJwt.php, but conventions say 'Don't add service or repository layers'. Input validation is hand-rolled (is_string/preg_match, is_int) rather than $request->validate, although that is defensible because the contract needs custom error codes. withCommands([TotemPairingCode::class]) (bootstrap/app.php:50-52) is redundant with command auto-discovery.

security.evidence: HS256 verification checks alg, compares with hash_equals, requires exp and rejects malformed base64 (TotemJwt.php:31-74). The secret must be set or a RuntimeException is thrown. The pairing code is never logged (only preset_id/entity_id/ip). No oracle: one 401 response for every failure case. Consumption happens under a row lock in a transaction. The entity is checked against claims, totem and preset, and queue scope is intersected with the current join. Queues are resolved inside the token entity only (TotemApiController.php:39-52). The CORS regex is anchored (#^https?://(?:localhost|127\.0\.0\.1)(?::\d+)?$#i), no credentials are sent, and Vary: Origin is set. Mass assignment uses explicit fillable plus forceFill for server-only fields.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/TotemApiTest.php covers: the pairing happy path with claim checks; a format dataset (missing, empty, short, long, letters, integer, padded); unknown/expired/consumed/inactive presets; single consumption; the 429 shape for auth and ticket; missing, tampered, expired and inactive tokens; forged entity claims; last_seen_at; queue filtering and order; immediate removal and no-grant-on-add; 404 for foreign slugs; 403 outside scope; inactive queue on both endpoints; sequential A001/A002 with channel totem; an invalid-priority dataset with no ticket created; CORS allow and deny plus the configured origin; the command's success and failure; and relationships. Missing: no assertion that the audit log is written or that it never contains the code, and no test that the code it replaces stops working for pairing.

simplicity.evidence: The change reuses IssueTicket. TotemPriorities is a single source for the endpoint and for validation. The HS256 implementation is small and allowed by the task. The shared TotemApiController base holds the guard and resolve logic once. Two things go further than needed. TotemVisuals reads per-preset appearance overrides (appearance['queues'][slug]['visual'|'color'|'icon'|'description'], TotemVisuals.php:20-36), which the task did not specify. The middleware validates queue claims element by element (AuthenticateTotem.php:63-71), which is more defensive than needed for a signed token.

readability.evidence: Classes are small and focused (TotemContext DTO, per-endpoint controllers, middleware). Names are clear, PHPDoc covers the public helpers, and comments explain non-obvious choices (bootstrap/app.php:33-39 on HandleCors and trimStrings). There is no dead code or debugging output, and the style matches sibling models (casts(), #[Fillable], typed relations).

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task. Some global changes reach beyond the totem endpoints: $middleware->remove(HandleCors::class) applies app-wide, and trimStrings is disabled for every api/* path (bootstrap/app.php:35-41). Both are justified in comments but affect future API routes. The appearance-override schema in TotemVisuals and its documentation (docs/api/totem.md) is extra presentation behaviour that was not asked for.

issues.explanation: The task requires audit logs for pairing success and failure that never include the full code, but no test asserts the audit log entries or the absence of the code in them.

The pairing command test checks that a new code is generated but not that the previous code now fails POST /api/totem/auth, so the 'regenerating replaces the previous code' requirement is only partly tested.
The conventions say not to add service layers, but the JWT helper is placed in a new App\Services namespace instead of App\Support, where the other helpers in this change live.
HandleCors is removed globally and string trimming is disabled for all api/* routes, which changes behaviour for any future API route, not just the totem endpoints.
Per-preset appearance overrides (color, icon, description keyed by queue slug) are speculative: the task does not define an appearance schema.
Registering TotemPairingCode through withCommands is redundant, because commands in app/Console/Commands are auto-discovered.
The failed-pairing audit log block is duplicated three times and could be one private helper.

review.summary: The change implements the totem BFF fully: migrations, models and factories, the pairing command, HS256 JWT pairing with a locked transaction, an auth middleware with the queue-scope intersection, the three scoped endpoints with ticket issuance through IssueTicket, an origin allow-list CORS policy, throttling with the rate_limited shape and synced docs, plus a thorough feature test suite. Remaining concerns are small: there are no tests for audit logging or for the replaced pairing code being rejected, the JWT helper sits in a Services namespace, two middleware changes apply app-wide, and the appearance overrides were not requested. I would approve with nits.
